# wallix.bastion.apikey

Manage API keys on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete an API key of the WALLIX Bastion REST API.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_apikey` Terraform resource.
- The Bastion generates the key value. It is returned once, when this module creates the key, in [`apikey.apikey`](#return-apikey-apikey), and can never be read again. See the notes.
- [`wallix.bastion.apikey_v2`](apikey_v2.md) manages the same keys with their profile and description.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-apikey-name"></a>**apikey_name** | `str` / required | Name of the API key. Identifies the key on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-ip-limitation"></a>**ip_limitation** | `str` | Comma-separated list of IP addresses, without spaces, allowed to use the key, for example `192.0.2.10,192.0.2.11`. an empty string allows any address. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the API key should exist.<br>With `absent`, make sure [`apikey_name`](#parameter-apikey-name) is not the key your own automation authenticates with.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- The key value is a secret. It is only returned by the run that creates the key, not in check mode. Set `no_log` to `true` on the task and store the value right away, for example in a vault.
- The Bastion gives the keys created by this module a default profile, visible with [`wallix.bastion.apikey_v2_info`](apikey_v2_info.md). Use [`wallix.bastion.apikey_v2`](apikey_v2.md) to choose it.
- Keys are created with the profile the Bastion gives them by default. Use [`wallix.bastion.apikey_v2`](apikey_v2.md) to choose it.
- To use the key, set [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) to its value and [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user) to a user of the Bastion.
- The key is looked up by [`apikey_name`](#parameter-apikey-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Create an API key for the CI pipeline
  wallix.bastion.apikey:
    apikey_name: ci-pipeline
    ip_limitation: 192.0.2.10,192.0.2.11
  register: ci_key
  no_log: true

- name: Store the key value, only known on creation
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    content: "{{ ci_key.apikey.apikey }}"
    dest: /root/.bastion-ci-key
    mode: "0600"
  when: ci_key.apikey.apikey is defined
  no_log: true

- name: Remove an API key
  wallix.bastion.apikey:
    apikey_name: ci-pipeline
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-apikey"></a>**apikey** | `dict` | The API key as returned by the Bastion API after the change.<br>In check mode, the expected key. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-apikey) |
| <a id="return-apikey-apikey"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **apikey** | `str` | The key value. Only returned when the key was created by this run; it can never be read again.<br><br>Returned: when the key was created, not in check mode<br><br>Sample: `EXAMPLE-api-key-returned-only-on-creation` |
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the key already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["ip_limitation"]` |

<a id="sample-apikey"></a>

### Sample of `apikey`

```yaml
apikey: EXAMPLE-api-key-returned-only-on-creation
apikey_name: ci-pipeline
id: 1a0f766d790f8b83005056b66c8b
ip_limitation: 192.0.2.10,192.0.2.11
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/apikeys/1a0f766d790f8b83005056b66c8b
```
